Question: In \(\triangle ABC\), \(D\) lies on \(BC\), \(BD:DC=1:2\), and \(E\) is the midpoint of \(AD\). Draw \(BE\) and extend it to intersect \(AC\) at \(F\). Find the value of \(AF/FC\). (Express the result as a fraction in lowest terms.)
Solution: Through \(D\), draw \(DG\parallel BF\), intersecting \(AC\) at \(G\). Since \(E\) is the midpoint of \(AD\) and \(EF\parallel DG\), \(AF=FG\). Also, since \(DG\parallel BF\), \(CG/GF=CD/DB=2\), giving \(GC=2FG\). Therefore, \(AF:FC=1:3\), and the value is \(1/3\).
